review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

14:1.sourceText: Τὸν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε, μὴ εἰς διακρίσεις διαλογισμῶν.
14:1.targetText: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἀσθενοῦντα ("the one being weak") is rendered him whose … is weak.
διακρίσεις ("disputes") is rendered passing judgment.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves εἰς ("for, leading to") untranslated in without passing judgment.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the Greek has none.

14:2.sourceText: ὃς μὲν πιστεύει φαγεῖν πάντα, ὁ δὲ ἀσθενῶν λάχανα ἐσθίει.
14:2.targetText: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

groups.note: πιστεύει ("believes") is rendered has faith.
The article with the participle ἀσθενῶν ("the one being weak") is rendered another, who is weak.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves μέν untranslated; the δέ that answers it is rendered while.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective to verse 1; the Greek has none here.
English adds only; the Greek says he eats vegetables.

14:3.sourceText: ὁ ἐσθίων τὸν μὴ ἐσθίοντα μὴ ἐξουθενείτω, ὁ δὲ μὴ ἐσθίων τὸν ἐσθίοντα μὴ κρινέτω, ὁ Θεὸς γὰρ αὐτὸν προσελάβετο.
14:3.targetText: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐσθίοντα ("eating") is rendered the one who does, standing for eat.
The article with the participle ἐσθίοντα ("eating") is rendered the one who does, standing for eat.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object from verse 2; the Greek has none.
English supplies the object from verse 2; the Greek has none.

14:4.sourceText: σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων ἀλλότριον οἰκέτην; τῷ ἰδίῳ κυρίῳ στήκει ἢ πίπτει· σταθήσεται δέ, δυνατεῖ γὰρ ὁ Κύριος στῆσαι αὐτόν.
14:4.targetText: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

groups.note: The article with the participle κρίνων ("the one judging") is rendered to judge.
The article τῷ is rendered as the possessive his.
στῆσαι ("to make stand") is rendered to make … stand.

14:5.sourceText: ὃς μὲν γὰρ κρίνει ἡμέραν παρ’ ἡμέραν, ὃς δὲ κρίνει πᾶσαν ἡμέραν· ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορείσθω.
14:5.targetText: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

groups.note: κρίνει ("judges") is rendered regards.
The second ἡμέραν ("day") is rendered the others.
κρίνει ("judges") is rendered considers.
The article τῷ is rendered as the possessive his.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves μέν untranslated; the δέ that answers it is rendered while.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds certain; the Greek says only "a day".
English adds alike; the Greek says "every day".

14:6.sourceText: ὁ φρονῶν τὴν ἡμέραν Κυρίῳ φρονεῖ· καὶ ὁ ἐσθίων Κυρίῳ ἐσθίει, εὐχαριστεῖ γὰρ τῷ Θεῷ· καὶ ὁ μὴ ἐσθίων Κυρίῳ οὐκ ἐσθίει, καὶ εὐχαριστεῖ τῷ Θεῷ.
14:6.targetText: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

groups.note: φρονεῖ ("regards it") is rendered does so.
ἐσθίει ("eats") is rendered does so.
ὁ μὴ ἐσθίων ("the one not eating") is rendered he who abstains.
οὐκ ἐσθίει ("does not eat") is rendered does so, pointing back to abstains.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB has no and here and starts a new clause with he who eats.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds special; the Greek has "the day".

14:7.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἑαυτῷ ζῇ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἑαυτῷ ἀποθνῄσκει·
14:7.targetText: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

groups.note: ἡμῶν ("of us") is understood again with the second οὐδείς, and BSB repeats it.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds alone; the Greek says "to himself".
English adds alone; the Greek says "to himself".

14:8.sourceText: ἐάν τε γὰρ ζῶμεν, τῷ Κυρίῳ ζῶμεν, ἐάν τε ἀποθνήσκωμεν, τῷ Κυρίῳ ἀποθνήσκομεν. ἐάν τε οὖν ζῶμεν ἐάν τε ἀποθνήσκωμεν, τοῦ Κυρίου ἐσμέν.
14:8.targetText: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

groups.note: The second ἐάν τε ("and if") is rendered or after whether.
ἐσμέν with the genitive ("we are the Lord's") is rendered we belong to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the first τε of ἐάν τε … ἐάν τε with a separate word.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB does not render the first τε of ἐάν τε … ἐάν τε with a separate word.

14:9.sourceText: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἔζησεν, ἵνα καὶ νεκρῶν καὶ ζώντων κυριεύσῃ.
14:9.targetText: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

groups.note: ἔζησεν ("lived") is rendered returned to life.

targetPhrases.text: He might be the Lord of

groups.note: κυριεύσῃ ("He might rule over") is rendered He might be the Lord of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated; For renders εἰς.

14:10.sourceText: Σὺ δὲ τί κρίνεις τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; ἢ καὶ σὺ τί ἐξουθενεῖς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; πάντες γὰρ παραστησόμεθα τῷ βήματι τοῦ Θεοῦ.
14:10.targetText: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

14:11.sourceText: γέγραπται γάρ Ζῶ ἐγώ, λέγει Κύριος, ὅτι ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ, καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσεται τῷ Θεῷ.
14:11.targetText: It is written:  “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

groups.note: ζῶ ἐγώ ("I live") is an oath formula, rendered As surely as I live.
ἐμοί ("to Me") is rendered before Me.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves ὅτι, which introduces what is sworn, untranslated.
BSB joins the two clauses with a semicolon and leaves καί untranslated.

14:12.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν ἕκαστος ἡμῶν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λόγον δώσει τῷ Θεῷ.
14:12.targetText: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:13.sourceText: Μηκέτι οὖν ἀλλήλους κρίνωμεν· ἀλλὰ τοῦτο κρίνατε μᾶλλον, τὸ μὴ τιθέναι πρόσκομμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἢ σκάνδαλον.
14:13.targetText: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

groups.note: μηκέτι ("no longer") is rendered stop.
ἀλλά … μᾶλλον ("but … rather") is rendered Instead.
κρίνατε ("decide") is rendered make up your mind.
The articular infinitive τὸ τιθέναι ("to put") is rendered to put.
The article τῷ is rendered as the possessive your.
The dative ἀδελφῷ ("for the brother") is rendered in … brother’s way.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τοῦτο ("this"), which points ahead to the infinitive clause, untranslated.

14:14.sourceText: οἶδα καὶ πέπεισμαι ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ ὅτι οὐδὲν κοινὸν δι’ ἑαυτοῦ· εἰ μὴ τῷ λογιζομένῳ τι κοινὸν εἶναι, ἐκείνῳ κοινόν.
14:14.targetText: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

groups.note: οἶδα ("I know") is rendered I am convinced.
εἰ μή ("except") is rendered But if.
The article with the participle λογιζομένῳ ("the one regarding") is rendered anyone regards.
The infinitive εἶναι ("to be") is rendered as.
ἐκείνῳ ("for that one") is rendered for him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.
English adds the adverb fully; πέπεισμαι means "I am persuaded".
English adds then to mark the result clause; the Greek has none.
English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek has none.

14:15.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ διὰ βρῶμα ὁ ἀδελφός σου λυπεῖται, οὐκέτι κατὰ ἀγάπην περιπατεῖς. μὴ τῷ βρώματί σου ἐκεῖνον ἀπόλλυε, ὑπὲρ οὗ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.
14:15.targetText: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

groups.note: βρῶμα ("food") is rendered what you eat.
περιπατεῖς ("you walk") is rendered you are acting.
βρώματι ("food") is rendered eating.
ἐκεῖνον ("that one") is rendered your brother.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:16.sourceText: μὴ βλασφημείσθω οὖν ὑμῶν τὸ ἀγαθόν.
14:16.targetText: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

targetPhrases.text: to be spoken of as evil

groups.note: The third-person imperative βλασφημείσθω ("let it be slandered") is rendered Do … allow … to be spoken of as evil.
ὑμῶν ("your") is rendered you in what you consider good.
The article τό, which makes ἀγαθόν a noun ("the good"), is rendered what.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds consider; the Greek says "your good".

14:17.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ βρῶσις καὶ πόσις, ἀλλὰ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ χαρὰ ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ·
14:17.targetText: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins righteousness and peace with a comma and leaves this καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a matter of; the Greek says the kingdom is not eating and drinking.
English repeats of from a matter of; the Greek has none.

14:18.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ δουλεύων τῷ Χριστῷ εὐάρεστος τῷ Θεῷ καὶ δόκιμος τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
14:18.targetText: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

groups.note: The article with the participle δουλεύων ("the one serving") is rendered whoever serves.
τούτῳ ("this") is rendered this way.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:19.sourceText: ἄρα οὖν τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης διώκομεν καὶ τὰ τῆς οἰκοδομῆς τῆς εἰς ἀλλήλους.
14:19.targetText: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

groups.note: The article τά ("the things") is rendered what.
Same verb; BSB's Greek has another form of it here, rendered let us pursue (N1904's indicative means "we pursue").

14:20.sourceText: μὴ ἕνεκεν βρώματος κατάλυε τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Θεοῦ. πάντα μὲν καθαρά, ἀλλὰ κακὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ διὰ προσκόμματος ἐσθίοντι.
14:20.targetText: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

groups.note: πάντα ("all things") is rendered All food.
κακόν ("evil, bad") is rendered wrong.

διὰ προσκόμματος ("with stumbling") is rendered a stumbling block.

14:21.sourceText: καλὸν τὸ μὴ φαγεῖν κρέα μηδὲ πιεῖν οἶνον μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἀδελφός σου προσκόπτει.

14:22.sourceText: σὺ πίστιν ἣν ἔχεις κατὰ σεαυτὸν ἔχε ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ. μακάριος ὁ μὴ κρίνων ἑαυτὸν ἐν ᾧ δοκιμάζει·
14:22.targetText: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

groups.note: σὺ … ἣν ἔχεις ("you … which you have") is rendered your.
κατὰ σεαυτὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ("to yourself before God") is rendered between yourself and God.

14:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ διακρινόμενος ἐὰν φάγῃ κατακέκριται, ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως· πᾶν δὲ ὃ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἁμαρτία ἐστίν.
14:23.targetText: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

groups.note: φάγῃ ("he eats") is understood again in the because-clause, and BSB repeats it as his eating.
